1.

learned counsel for the appellant.
None for the respondents-claimants.
Accordingly, the Court has proceeded to hear the learned counsel for the appellant.

2. The instant appeal has been preferred under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 assailing the judgment and award dated 21.10.2004 whereby the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal has allowed the Claim Petition No.41/2001 awarding a sum of Rs.1,02,000/- along with 6% interest in favour of the claimants-respondents.

sentences.text: 3. Assailing the aforesaid award, the submission of the learned counsel for the appellant is that there is a diversion in the statement given by the claimants-respondents in the claim petition as well as in the statement recorded in his deposition.

4. It is further stated that the evidence of the defendants has not been considered inasmuch as DW-1, the driver of the bus concerned has not been noticed, as a result, incorrect findings have been recorded, which has vitiated the award.
5. Before considering the aforesaid submissions, it will be appropriate to take note of certain brief facts giving rise to the instant appeal.

6. The record indicates that a Claim Petition No.41/2001 was filed by the parents of the deceased,
who was a young child and while he was on his way to school, a bus belonging to the appellant,
bearing UP-32-6248 was being driven rashly and negligently which caused the accident and as such the child expired.
7.
Upon exchange of the pleadings, the Tribunal had framed three issues.

The first issue related as to whether the accident was caused by rash and negligent driving of the bus driver, resulting in the accident and the other issues relating to the fact whether the driver of the bus was having a valid and subsisting licence.

8. On behalf of the claimants witnesses were examined, who clearly deposed that the deceased was studying in Class-V and was on his way to school when the bus was driven rashly and negligently and hit the young body on account of which he expired.

9. Refuting the aforesaid, the bus driver was examined as DW-1 and thereafter considering the oral and the documentary evidence, the Tribunal by means of its award dated 21.10.2004 awarded a sum of Rs.1,02,000/- along with 6% interest in favour of the claimants-respondents.

10. In the aforesaid backdrop, if the submission of the learned counsel for the appellant is tested in light of the material available on record, it is a clear case of the claimants-respondents that the deceased being a young boy was on his way to school when he was hit by the bus and he expired.
Minor discrepancy in the statement does not affect the merits of the matter.

The minor difference is not to be taken in a pedantic fashion so as to deprive the compensation to the claimants which is part of the beneficial legislation for the survivors or heirs/dependents of the deceased of motor accident.
11. Insofar as the claimants-respondents are concerned, from examining the witnesses, they have also filed documentary evidence regarding the child studying in school.

His academic records indicates that he was good in studies as well as documents relating to a criminal case which was registered in pursuance of the FIR/Case Crime No.72/2001.
12.

The record further indicates that insofar as the documentary evidence is concerned, no documentary evidence was filed by the Corporation to dispute the fact that the DW-1, who was the Regional Manager U.P.Staate Road ... vs Vishwanath And 4 Ors.

2 driver of the bus, he was apprehended.
The driver had to take bail and even the bus in question was seized by the police.
The driver was charge-sheeted and while he was cross-examined, he has admitted the aforesaid facts.

13. It is now well settled to be disputed that the claim petitions under the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal are to be decided on the basis of preponderance of probabilities and the pedantic approach to screen the evidence is not to be followed.
14.

In the instant case, once the foundational facts were duly supported and proved by the evidence,
it was for the Corporation to have led credible and convincing evidence to disprove the stand of the claimants which unfortunately has not been done.
15. For the aforesaid reasons, this Court does not find that there is any error committed by the Tribunal while decreeing the claim by means of its award dated 21.10.2004.
Accordingly, the appeal is without merits and is dismissed.
The costs are made easy.
16. Any amount deposited before this Court shall be released in favour of the claimants-respondents.
Any amount which is left shall also be paid with up-to-date interest by the Corporation to the claimants-respondents within a period of six weeks from today in terms of the award.
17. The record of the Tribunal concerned shall be remitted forthwith.
